title: [Core]: Improve `ObjectDB` multi-threading performance and safety
body:
## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

- Supersedes: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/118803
- Closes: https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/15362
- Closes: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/65404
- Makes `ObjectDB::get_ref` fully thread-safe by removing the short window when the pointer could be freed.
- Removes a possible UB in `ObjectDB::debug_objects`. While we are inside the spin lock other threads can try to delete objects, which will make them wait in `ObjectDB::remove_instance`. The problem is that `ObjectDB::remove_instance` is inside the base `Object` destructor, so objects that wait here can only access `Object` members (see `Node::print_orphan_nodes` accessing `Node`) because the derived parts of the object were destroyed. It now only passes instances outside of predelete, so all members from derived classes are still valid.

Small issues this PR also happens to fix:
- Closes: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/109178
- Closes: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/111173

Related issue: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/58279, I think it is already fixed in master in the release template.

## Additional information

Overview of changes:
- Use double array to newer deallocate slots after allocating them, gets rid of `realloc` so we can always access valid slots.
- Store the data as atomic inside the slot and use it as a slot's spin lock. Any changes or readings to the slot are now local to the slot's spin lock, so it won't content with other slots. Calling `ObjectDB::get_instance` on the same slot is still as slow as before, but calling it on different slots is now uncontentious.
- Use thread local queues for slot reuse. They are segmented to not allow any thread to hold on too many slots locally, i.e. when there are too many slots it pushes the segment to a global queues array, when it is empty it gets a new segment.
- Adds `ObjectDB::get_locked_instance` that will return pointer and prevent it from being deleted until it's unlocked. Returned pointer also counts as an active slot reader until unlocked.

The main speed benefits comes from the thread local queues and moving from a global lock to a slot local one.
Basically less global contentions.

<details>
<summary>Where ObjectDB::get_instance being used in the GDScript VM:</summary>

- `OPCODE_SET_KEYED` leads to `VariantKeyedSetGetObject::set` (validated setter) with Object

- `OPCODE_ASSIGN_TYPED_SCRIPT`

- `OPCODE_CAST_TO_NATIVE`

- `OPCODE_CALL_RETURN`
- `OPCODE_CALL`

- `OPCODE_SET_NAMED` leads to `Variant::set_named` with Object

### Design decisions

- Avoids bit-fields for data, because how they are stored and their is implementation defined for all platforms, but we need the data to be stored very explicitly, also it is easier to use the lower 24 bits for different purposes if the data is dynamically unpacked.
- When the slot is active the lower 24 bits are used for a readers count, only `ObjectDB::get_locked_instance` adds them, so it is impossible to run out of space for readers in practice. Inactive slots store the next slot's index in the free slots queue.
- `ObjectDB::get_locked_instance` was added after reading in https://redirect.github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/121936 that we don't have any way to provide thread safety for returned non-refcounted objects. It was also useful for `ObjectDB::debug_objects` as it allows to lock the instance and keep the slot itself unlocked, now `DebugFunc` can freely call into `ObjectDB` and keep working.
- This PR doesn't change how `ObjectDB::get_instance` works from outside of the `ObjectDB`. It is as safe as the current version, which is to say it's not really that safe, but it's also not that unsafe.

### Considerations
- Because of a virtual queues it has 1 less usable slot (I needed to treat 1 usable index as null).
- If more than 8192 threads exists at the same time and called `ObjectDB::add_instance`, it is possible to run out of slots as when thread local queues take them, they take segments for speed. When the thread local queue is destroyed with the thread exit it pushes segments back to the global queues array, so this worry is unrealistic. It is also possible to shrink validator bits to store more slots or reduce the queue segment size if necessary.
- Single-threaded performance is slightly slower as `ObjectDB` now needs to do more things to support multi-threading, except when it creates and frees a large number of objects at the same time (see `func_new_groups`). In majority of other cases even 2 threads nets you a large increase in speed compared to before, except when creating `GDScriptInstance` (every new one locks a global mutex).
- `ObjectDB::debug_objects` can be inaccurate now, as during the iteration it is possible to add new instances, it is still fully thread-safe.
- Tbh `ObjectDB::get_locked_instance` can be removed, it was just something that seemed nice to have, something like that will be still used inside the `ObjectDB` for a nicer `ObjectDB::debug_objects`.

## Benchmark

The results are in tables with numbers measuring ns/op. The columns indicate how many threads were used for that run. Each run had the same workload that was split between running threads. 

Project: [testthreads4.6_2026-09-26_17-47-06.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33029651/testthreads4.6_2026-09-26_17-47-06.zip)

<details>
<summary>Tested with</summary>

Compile commands:
```
scons target=editor use_llvm=yes linker=lld optimize=speed debug_symbols=yes accesskit=no tests=yes lto=none
scons target=template_release optimize=speed accesskit=no use_llvm=yes linker=lld production=yes
```

<details>
<summary>Code</summary>

<details>
<summary>func_base</summary>

```gdscript
func func_base(count: int) -> int:
	var sum := 0
	if sem: sem.wait()
	var time_start := Time.get_ticks_usec()
	for i in count:
		sum = 1
	var time_end := Time.get_ticks_usec()
	finished.emit.call_deferred(time_end - time_start)
	return sum
```
</details>
<details>
<summary>func_get</summary>

```gdscript
func func_get(count: int) -> int:
	var sum := 0
	var obj := HelperObj.new()
	if sem: sem.wait()
	var time_start := Time.get_ticks_usec()
	for i in count:
		sum = obj.increment
	var time_end := Time.get_ticks_usec()
	obj.free()
	finished.emit.call_deferred(time_end - time_start)
	return sum
```
</details>
<details>
<summary>func_set</summary>

```gdscript
func func_set(count: int) -> int:
	var obj := HelperObj.new()
	if sem: sem.wait()
	var time_start := Time.get_ticks_usec()
	for i in count:
		obj.value = i
	var value := obj.value
	var time_end := Time.get_ticks_usec()
	obj.free()
	finished.emit.call_deferred(time_end - time_start)
	return value
```
</details>
<details>
<summary>call_base</summary>

```gdscript
func call_base(count: int) -> int:
	var sum := 0
	if sem: sem.wait()
	var time_start := Time.get_ticks_usec()
	for i in count:
		sum = get_instance_increment()
	var time_end := Time.get_ticks_usec()
	finished.emit.call_deferred(time_end - time_start)
	return sum

func get_instance_increment() -> int:
	return 1
```
</details>
<details>
<summary>func_get_instance_from_id</summary>

```gdscript
var obj_instance_id: int
func func_get_instance_from_id(count: int) -> int:
	if sem: sem.wait()
	var time_start := Time.get_ticks_usec()
	for i in count:
		var _obj: Object = instance_from_id(obj_instance_id)
	var time_end := Time.get_ticks_usec()
	finished.emit.call_deferred(time_end - time_start)
	return 0
```
</details>
<details>
<summary>func_new_obj</summary>

```gdscript
func func_new_obj(count: int) -> int:
	if sem: sem.wait()
	var time_start := Time.get_ticks_usec()
	for i in count:
		var obj := Object.new()
		obj.free()
	var time_end := Time.get_ticks_usec()
	finished.emit.call_deferred(time_end - time_start)
	return count
```
</details>
<details>
<summary>func_new_script</summary>

```gdscript
func func_new_script(count: int) -> int:
	if sem: sem.wait()
	var time_start := Time.get_ticks_usec()
	for i in count:
		var obj := HelperObj.new()
		obj.free()
	var time_end := Time.get_ticks_usec()
	finished.emit.call_deferred(time_end - time_start)
	return count
```
</details>
<details>
<summary>func_new_groups</summary>

```gdscript
func func_new_groups(count: int) -> int:
	var groups_count: int = 10
	@warning_ignore("integer_division")
	var obj_count: int = count / groups_count
	var holder: Array[Object]
	holder.resize(obj_count)
	if sem: sem.wait()
	var time_start := Time.get_ticks_usec()
	for _group in groups_count:
		for i in obj_count:
			holder[i] = Object.new()
		for i in obj_count:
			holder[i].free()
	var time_end := Time.get_ticks_usec()
	finished.emit.call_deferred(time_end - time_start)
	return obj_count
```
</details>
</details>
